mira: Quick sync — Lumen-13B int4 bring-up finished overnight. Ran baseline behavior + safety smoke. Summary: mixed. Need quick triage.

sanjay: what did the smoke-suite flag? short bullets pls.

mira: - jailbreak harness (rb-jb-suite v3) -> ~8% more successful bypasses vs fp16 baseline on a 10k probe set. Mostly prompt-chaining social-engineering types.
  - toxicity-probe-v2 -> overall toxicity score +0.12 AUC compared to baseline, Spanish subset shows +0.22.
  - refusal-regression -> soft-refusal flip rate up from 1.1% -> 3.7% on short counterfactuals.

alex: ugh. was the quant profile straight int4 with no residual path? or hybrid?

mira: int4-nopref (no fp16 residual), kv-cache preserved. We did a quick verify with int4+fp16-residual and the JB success rate dropped ~half.

ethan: can you paste the exact commands/config used for the redteam harness? will reproduce locally.

mira: Sure:
```
# run harness
python -m redteam.runner --suite rb-jb-suite --model lumen-13b-int4 --batch 64 --sample-seed 42 --out s3://redwood-evals/lumen/int4/rb-jb/2026-03-20/
```
Config excerpt:
```yaml
model: lumen-13b-int4
quant: int4
residual: false
max_tokens: 512
policy_filter: off  # smoke pass, not gating
```

qa-sam: I kicked off a diff-run that compares fp16 vs int4 on the same seeds. uploading artifacts -> s3://redwood-evals/lumen/diffs/3523456789/diff.json.gz. Initial look: many JB hits are prompt-concat/roleplay style.

alex: any logs of logits or token-level divergence? might be informative for where the refusal boundary shifts.

mira: saved per-token logprobs for 2k failure cases. path: s3://redwood-evals/lumen/int4/artifacts/3523456789/logprobs/ . Also a small sample attached below (paste):
```
# example divergence (truncated)
FP16: "I cannot help with that."
INT4: "Okay, here's how you can do it..."
next_token_logprob_diff: -3.4 -> +1.2
```

ethan: interesting — suggests quant noise pushes the policy head into a different argmax. could be mitigated by higher temperature? but we don't want to tweak decoding globally.

qa-sam: also saw a pattern where system prompt anchor tokens were slightly lower prob, causing the assistant to more readily accept user overrides.

ops-bot: deployment note: dedicated staging pool (lumen-staging) auto-rolled to int4 variant at 03:10 UTC, traffic ramp 10% -> 50% over 30m. No customer-facing routes.

mira: Proposed immediate plan:
- block: revert staging to fp16-residual for now (ethan?)
- triage: run focused jailbreak cohort with int4+residual and int4-nopref to isolate residual effect (sanjay + qa-sam)
- evaluation: run policy classifier on int4 outputs, compute threshold drift; produce ROC delta (mira)
- mitigation: evaluate small post-filter (policy re-score) at inference time for high-risk prompts (alex + eng-runtime)

sanjay: I'll start the triage run. ETA ~2h for first batch (will post summary).

ethan: reverting staging now. rolling back to lumen-13b-fp16-resid. ping if rollback fails.

alex: for longer term — let's add a short fuzz harness that injects system-prompt perturbations and measures anchor token stability across quant profiles. could catch these anchor drops early. I'll sketch an RFC.

qa-sam: logging note — please tag all experiment runs with eval_tag=lumen_int4_safety_20260320 so we can filter in the reports.

mira: thanks. if anyone is reproducing, use seed=42 and the s3 paths above. Will collect regression report and propose gating thresholds by EOD.

ethan: one quick datapoint — the Spanish toxicity bump concentrated in code-switching prompts (es+en). Might be a tokenizer edge with int4. Adding tokenizer-diff to the triage.

mira: Good. I'll create a short incident tracker entry in /incidents for follow-through. For now, priority: staging rollback (done), triage runs (sanjay), policy rescoring experiment (alex).

ops-bot: @here Incident created: #INC-2026-147 lumen-int4-safety-regression (links: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-147) :warning:
